task: Identify the shared handler reached by the defined uv_getaddrinfo, uv_freeaddrinfo and uv_spawn export stubs; no whole-native investigation.

conclusion.confidence: high, based on original native instructions and original referenced constant bytes
conclusion.statement: The three named exports replace the first argument with their own fixed function name and call a shared handler that uses the exact literal unsupported uv function: with the name as a formatting argument. They are unsupported libuv API stubs, not implementations of the advertised DNS/process operations.
does_not_establish: The normal internal Bun or Claude DNS/execution route.
That all DNS traffic calls the imported getaddrinfo symbol or passes a Termux interposer.
The exact runtime termination, error return or exception behavior of the handler.
Whether the real Claude runtime calls any of these exported stubs.

observations.observation: uv_getaddrinfo loads x0 with address 0x25e33d, whose original ELF bytes are uv_getaddrinfo followed by NUL; BL 0x2a7ca20.
uv_freeaddrinfo and uv_spawn use their own fixed function-name strings and the same BL target 0x2a7ca20.
Shared wrapper calls 0x3325d00; next decoded instruction is UDF #0.
mov x19,x0 preserves the supplied function-name pointer.
mov x0,x19; BL 0x4d054c0 (validated strlen PLT); store returned name length at [x29-0x18].
ADRP x1,0x227000; ADD x1,x1,#0x5ce places the formatting-constant pointer 0x2275ce in x1.
The original name pointer is stored at [x29-0x20], paired with its length, and referenced through the argument storage passed in x2.
BL 0x3329640 receives x0 pointing to stack output/storage, x1 pointing to the unsupported-UV constant, and x2 pointing to the name formatting argument.
Two further direct calls target 0x3326940 and 0x3326c40; their complete behavior was not traced.

referenced_constant.format_type: Opaque constant with control bytes, not asserted to be a plain NUL-terminated C string.

limitations: Global automatic analysis and no-return inference were disabled. The 512-byte range is not claimed as a complete function body.
The output after 0x3325dd0 may include adjacent code reached by treating an unknown non-returning call as returning; no conclusion relies on that tail.
The decisive name/literal/argument/call sequence is before that possible boundary overrun.
No large xref scan, guessed function-body creation, decompilation of an artificial partial function, or target execution was needed.
Preliminary raw ADRP/ADD candidates include addresses beyond the trusted sequence; only the constant actually used in the shown instruction trace supports the conclusion.
